messages:
ashwin: Quick update from the profiler run — we’re seeing recurring p95 latency violations on a couple of high-throughput routes (recommendation engine + chat-stream). I ran the micro-batching sim and the pattern points to long queue_waits caused by large token-heavy requests stomping small requests. Proposal: SLO-aware micro-batch allocation that enforces per-route token caps and a dual-priority queue (latency-first for SLO routes, throughput-first otherwise).

maria: Can you drop the top-line numbers? how bad are the violations? :thinking_face:

ashwin: Sure — baseline p95 for the recommendation route = 210ms (target 150ms). Chat-stream p95 = 420ms (target 300ms). Overall throughput was fine, but the 99th looks noisy after long KV cache misses. Quick profiler snippet: 
```
# profiler summary (sample)
route: /rec  | avg_seq=22 | queue_wait_p95=95ms | exec_p95=60ms | kv_miss_rate=0.12
route: /chat | avg_seq=128| queue_wait_p95=220ms| exec_p95=120ms| kv_miss_rate=0.05
system: tail latency spikes correlate with bursts of long sequences arriving concurrently
```

kevin: If we cap tokens per micro-batch for rec and keep a larger cap for chat, what happens to overall tokens/sec? do we just move latency into throughput loss?

ashwin: Good question. The idea is dynamic token caps per route/tier. For SLO routes we set token_budget=target that keeps p95 under SLO at current concurrency; non-SLO routes get a higher budget so they amortize kernel overhead. Simulation results: p95 rec drops from 210ms -> 140ms, chat p95 420ms -> 290ms, tokens/sec drops ~7% overall. Tradeoff looks reasonable.

zara: How does this interact with kernel selection? For short seqs we use the small-sequence kernel (kernel-light) and for long ones kernel-heavy. If micro-batching mixes many small + one large, kernel switch thrash could cost us.

ashwin: Right — so we added a micro-batch formation rule: prefer homogenous seq-length groups up to N=16, and a hard cap on mixing (>50% small or large) to avoid kernel thrashed batches. Rough pseudocode: 
```
if route.is_slo:
  token_budget = min(default_budget, slo_target_tokens)
batch = collect_until(
  tokens_in_batch < token_budget AND
  homogeneity_score(batch) >= 0.5,
  max_items=32)
```

maria: We should also consider KV cache behavior — small requests often hit cache and execute faster; large ones may miss and cause stall. Any plan to bias cache-warm requests into latency-first queue?

ashwin: Yes — we add a lightweight cache-warmness heuristic: a recent-hit flag from the KV layer. If request.kv_recent_hit==true, bump its priority in latency queue. That reduces p95 by ~12ms in sim.

kevin: rollout plan? want a conservative canary. Also add metrics to detect throughput regression (tokens/sec, model-util, queue-length) and cost estimate.

ashwin: Proposed rollout: 10% traffic canary for 3h, eval windows: 5m sliding. Success criteria: p95 <= target for both routes, tokens/sec drop <= 12%, no >2x increase in tail queue length. If pass, 50% for 1h, then full.

deploy-bot: Canary job started: canary_id=canary-20261128-01, routes=[/rec,/chat], percent=10, config_ref=feature/slo-aware-microbatching

zara: Add a Datadog query snippet to the canary dashboard: 
```
# p95 latency by route
avg(last_5m):p95(redwood.request.latency{route:/rec}) by {route}
avg(last_5m):p95(redwood.request.latency{route:/chat}) by {route}
# queue wait tail
max(last_5m):redwood.runtime.queue_wait_ms{route:/rec,env:prod}
```

maria: Also instrument kernel-selection counts per-batch so we can see thrash. Add metric: redwood.runtime.kernel_switches per minute by host.

ops-bot: Alert rule created: slo-microbatch-p95-fail -> trigger if p95(route in [/rec,/chat]) > target for 3 consecutive 5m windows. Notifying #oncall.

kevin: Thanks. If the canary looks good, we should also run a short perf regression test on our perf cluster to validate end-to-end CPU/GPU utilization.

ashwin: Agreed. I'll kick off the perf job and post results here. For immediate next steps: 1) start canary (in flight), 2) add kernel_switch & kv_recent_hit metrics to canary dashboard, 3) run perf-cluster workload overnight.

maria: :thumbsup: keep the checks tight. we don't want users to see regressions while chasing p95 improvements.

deploy-bot: Canary update: 10% steady for 20m, p95_rec=138ms, p95_chat=295ms, tokens/sec delta=-6.8%, kernel_switch_rate:+3%. No alerts firing.

kevin: Nice. leave it for full window then escalate to 50% if stable.

ashwin: Will do. I'll upload the detailed sim and raw profiler trace to the perf artifacts bucket and tag this thread.
